# GBLUP models for the real-data analysis

## 1. Objective

This module fits three nested genomic best linear unbiased prediction models
under the common outer validation design:

\[
\text{GBLUP-A}: \quad y = \mu + a + \varepsilon,
\]

\[
\text{GBLUP-AD}: \quad y = \mu + a + d + \varepsilon,
\]

and

\[
\text{GBLUP-ADE}: \quad y = \mu + a + d + aa + \varepsilon.
\]

The three structures are evaluated independently in exactly the same outer
splits. Increasing model complexity is therefore treated as an empirical
question: dominance and epistatic components are retained as candidate
structures, but predictive superiority is not assumed from model completeness.

The response in every task is the individual BLUP obtained in the longitudinal
phenotype module. The 39 BLUPs assigned to the outer assessment set are masked
before model fitting and are used only for held-out evaluation.

## 2. Computational setup

```{r setup-gblup}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(
  library(sommer)
)

suppressPackageStartupMessages(
  library(ggplot2)
)

suppressPackageStartupMessages(
  library(ggthemes)
)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE
)

RUN_GBLUP <- identical(
  Sys.getenv("RUN_GBLUP"),
  "1"
)

SEED_GLOBAL <- 20261105L
N_ITERS_SOMMER <- 50L
TOL_LLIK <- 1e-4

COMMON_PATH <-
  "output/real/audit/preprocessed_real_common.rds"

VALIDATION_PATH <-
  "output/real/validation/real_cv_design.rds"

OUTPUT_DIR <-
  "output/real/gblup"

FIGURE_DIR <-
  file.path(
    OUTPUT_DIR,
    "figures"
  )

RESULTS_RDS <-
  file.path(
    OUTPUT_DIR,
    "real_gblup_results.rds"
  )

RESULTS_CSV <-
  file.path(
    OUTPUT_DIR,
    "real_gblup_results.csv"
  )

PREDICTIONS_RDS <-
  file.path(
    OUTPUT_DIR,
    "real_gblup_predictions.rds"
  )

PREDICTIONS_CSV <-
  file.path(
    OUTPUT_DIR,
    "real_gblup_predictions.csv"
  )

KERNEL_SUMMARY_CSV <-
  file.path(
    OUTPUT_DIR,
    "real_gblup_kernel_summary.csv"
  )

NUMERICAL_SUMMARY_CSV <-
  file.path(
    OUTPUT_DIR,
    "real_gblup_numerical_summary.csv"
  )

PERFORMANCE_SUMMARY_CSV <-
  file.path(
    OUTPUT_DIR,
    "real_gblup_performance_summary.csv"
  )

RUN_METADATA_RDS <-
  file.path(
    OUTPUT_DIR,
    "real_gblup_run_metadata.rds"
  )

RANKING_RDS <-
  file.path(
    OUTPUT_DIR,
    "real_gblup_individual_ranking.rds"
  )

RANKING_CSV <-
  file.path(
    OUTPUT_DIR,
    "real_gblup_individual_ranking.csv"
  )

RANKING_SUMMARY_CSV <-
  file.path(
    OUTPUT_DIR,
    "real_gblup_ranking_summary.csv"
  )

dir.create(
  OUTPUT_DIR,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

dir.create(
  FIGURE_DIR,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)
```

The same numerical controls are used for the three structures. No model is
changed after inspecting an outer assessment set, and no split-specific
hyperparameter search is performed.

## 3. Common genomic object and validation design

```{r load-common-validation}
stopifnot(
  file.exists(COMMON_PATH),
  file.exists(VALIDATION_PATH)
)

common <- readRDS(
  COMMON_PATH
)

cv <- readRDS(
  VALIDATION_PATH
)

geno <- as.matrix(
  common$genotype
)

blups <- common$phenotype
traits <- common$traits
ids <- rownames(geno)

stopifnot(
  identical(
    traits,
    c(
      "Cer",
      "BM",
      "LP"
    )
  ),
  nrow(geno) == 195L,
  ncol(geno) == 20887L,
  length(ids) == 195L,
  !anyDuplicated(ids),
  all(
    c(
      "Phenotype_ID",
      "Cer",
      "BM",
      "LP"
    ) %in%
      names(blups)
  )
)

phenotype_ids <- as.character(
  blups$Phenotype_ID
)

stopifnot(
  identical(
    phenotype_ids,
    ids
  )
)

outer_meta <- unique(
  cv$outer_assignments[
    ,
    c(
      "Repetition",
      "OuterFold",
      "SplitID"
    )
  ]
)

outer_meta <- outer_meta[
  order(
    outer_meta$Repetition,
    outer_meta$OuterFold
  ),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

rownames(
  outer_meta
) <- NULL

stopifnot(
  nrow(outer_meta) == 25L,
  length(
    unique(
      outer_meta$SplitID
    )
  ) == 25L
)

input_summary <- data.frame(
  Item = c(
    "Individuals",
    "Markers after QC",
    "Traits",
    "Outer splits",
    "Outer analysis size",
    "Outer assessment size",
    "Candidate GBLUP structures"
  ),
  Value = c(
    nrow(geno),
    ncol(geno),
    length(traits),
    nrow(outer_meta),
    156L,
    39L,
    3L
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

input_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Common inputs used by the GBLUP models",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%;"'
  )
```

The validation object is consumed without modification. Consequently, A, AD,
and ADE are compared on identical training and held-out individuals.

## 4. Genomic relationship matrices

The three covariance structures are built once from the frozen 20,887-marker
matrix and reused throughout the 225 model fits.

The additive matrix represents realized additive relationships. The dominance
matrix represents realized dominance relationships. The epistatic matrix is the
additive-by-additive genomic relationship matrix.

```{r build-kernels, eval=RUN_GBLUP}
kernel_start <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]

A_matrix <- sommer::A.mat(
  geno,
  min.MAF = 0
)

D_matrix <- sommer::D.mat(
  geno,
  nishio = TRUE,
  min.MAF = 0
)

E_matrix <- sommer::E.mat(
  geno,
  nishio = TRUE,
  type = "A#A",
  min.MAF = 0
)

kernel_seconds <-
  proc.time()[["elapsed"]] -
  kernel_start

rownames(A_matrix) <- ids
colnames(A_matrix) <- ids

rownames(D_matrix) <- ids
colnames(D_matrix) <- ids

rownames(E_matrix) <- ids
colnames(E_matrix) <- ids

kernel_summary <- data.frame(
  Kernel = c(
    "Additive",
    "Dominance",
    "Epistatic_AxA"
  ),
  Rows = c(
    nrow(A_matrix),
    nrow(D_matrix),
    nrow(E_matrix)
  ),
  Columns = c(
    ncol(A_matrix),
    ncol(D_matrix),
    ncol(E_matrix)
  ),
  Symmetric = c(
    isTRUE(
      all.equal(
        A_matrix,
        t(A_matrix),
        tolerance = 1e-8
      )
    ),
    isTRUE(
      all.equal(
        D_matrix,
        t(D_matrix),
        tolerance = 1e-8
      )
    ),
    isTRUE(
      all.equal(
        E_matrix,
        t(E_matrix),
        tolerance = 1e-8
      )
    )
  ),
  Finite = c(
    all(
      is.finite(
        A_matrix
      )
    ),
    all(
      is.finite(
        D_matrix
      )
    ),
    all(
      is.finite(
        E_matrix
      )
    )
  ),
  Mean_diagonal = c(
    mean(
      diag(
        A_matrix
      )
    ),
    mean(
      diag(
        D_matrix
      )
    ),
    mean(
      diag(
        E_matrix
      )
    )
  ),
  Kernel_build_seconds = rep(
    kernel_seconds,
    3L
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

stopifnot(
  all(
    kernel_summary$Rows == 195L
  ),
  all(
    kernel_summary$Columns == 195L
  ),
  all(
    kernel_summary$Symmetric
  ),
  all(
    kernel_summary$Finite
  )
)

write.csv(
  kernel_summary,
  KERNEL_SUMMARY_CSV,
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r load-kernel-summary, eval=!RUN_GBLUP}
stopifnot(
  file.exists(
    KERNEL_SUMMARY_CSV
  )
)

kernel_summary <- read.csv(
  KERNEL_SUMMARY_CSV,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
```

```{r show-kernel-summary}
kernel_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 6,
    caption = "Genomic relationship matrices used by the three GBLUP structures",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%;"'
  )
```

## 5. Fixed candidate structures

The model structures are fixed before assessment performance is inspected.

```{r model-contract}
model_contract <- data.frame(
  Structure = c(
    "A",
    "AD",
    "ADE"
  ),
  Model = c(
    "GBLUP_A",
    "GBLUP_AD",
    "GBLUP_ADE"
  ),
  Genomic_components = c(
    "Additive",
    "Additive + dominance",
    "Additive + dominance + additive-by-additive epistasis"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

model_contract |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Fixed GBLUP candidate structures",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%;"'
  )
```

The model comparison therefore evaluates whether additional genomic components
improve prediction. The most complete structure is not assumed to be the best
predictive structure.

## 6. Evaluation grid

Three traits, 25 outer splits, and three fixed GBLUP structures produce 225
independent fitting tasks.

```{r task-grid}
task_table <- data.frame(
  Dataset = character(0),
  Trait = character(0),
  Repetition = integer(0),
  OuterFold = integer(0),
  SplitID = character(0),
  Structure = character(0),
  Model = character(0),
  TaskID = character(0),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

for (trait in traits) {

  for (
    split_row in
      seq_len(
        nrow(
          outer_meta
        )
      )
  ) {

    for (
      model_row in
        seq_len(
          nrow(
            model_contract
          )
        )
    ) {

      task_table <- rbind(
        task_table,
        data.frame(
          Dataset = "real",
          Trait = trait,
          Repetition =
            outer_meta$Repetition[
              split_row
            ],
          OuterFold =
            outer_meta$OuterFold[
              split_row
            ],
          SplitID =
            outer_meta$SplitID[
              split_row
            ],
          Structure =
            model_contract$Structure[
              model_row
            ],
          Model =
            model_contract$Model[
              model_row
            ],
          TaskID = paste(
            trait,
            outer_meta$SplitID[
              split_row
            ],
            model_contract$Structure[
              model_row
            ],
            sep = "_"
          ),
          stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )
      )
    }
  }
}

rownames(
  task_table
) <- NULL

stopifnot(
  nrow(task_table) == 225L,
  length(
    unique(
      task_table$TaskID
    )
  ) == 225L,
  all(
    table(
      task_table$Trait
    ) == 75L
  ),
  all(
    table(
      task_table$Structure
    ) == 75L
  )
)

task_summary <- as.data.frame(
  table(
    task_table$Trait,
    task_table$Structure
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

names(
  task_summary
) <- c(
  "Trait",
  "Structure",
  "Tasks"
)

task_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Number of outer fitting tasks by trait and GBLUP structure",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%;"'
  )
```

## 7. Fit A, AD, and ADE in every outer split

For each task, the 39 assessment BLUPs are replaced by `NA` before fitting. The
model therefore receives all genomic relationships but no held-out response
information.

All three structures use the same `sommer::mmes()` fitting controls. Numerical
diagnostics are recorded for inspection but do not trigger split-specific model
changes.

```{r fit-all-gblup-models, eval=RUN_GBLUP}
set.seed(
  SEED_GLOBAL
)

run_start <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]

result_list <- vector(
  "list",
  nrow(task_table)
)

prediction_list <- vector(
  "list",
  nrow(task_table)
)

for (
  i in
    seq_len(
      nrow(
        task_table
      )
    )
) {

  task <- task_table[
    i,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  trait <- task$Trait
  structure <- task$Structure

  split <- cv$outer_splits[[
    task$SplitID
  ]]

  analysis_index <- match(
    split$analysis_ids,
    ids
  )

  assessment_index <- match(
    split$assessment_ids,
    ids
  )

  stopifnot(
    length(
      analysis_index
    ) == 156L,
    length(
      assessment_index
    ) == 39L,
    !anyNA(
      analysis_index
    ),
    !anyNA(
      assessment_index
    ),
    length(
      intersect(
        analysis_index,
        assessment_index
      )
    ) == 0L
  )

  response_vector <- blups[[
    trait
  ]]

  id_factor <- factor(
    ids,
    levels = ids
  )

  dat <- data.frame(
    y = response_vector,
    id = id_factor,
    idd = id_factor,
    ide = id_factor
  )

  dat$y[
    assessment_index
  ] <- NA_real_

  fit_start <- proc.time()[[
    "elapsed"
  ]]

  if (
    structure == "A"
  ) {

    fit <- sommer::mmes(
      y ~ 1,
      random = ~
        vsm(
          ism(id),
          Gu = A_matrix
        ),
      rcov = ~ units,
      nIters = N_ITERS_SOMMER,
      tolParConvLL = TOL_LLIK,
      data = dat,
      verbose = FALSE,
      dateWarning = FALSE
    )

  } else if (
    structure == "AD"
  ) {

    fit <- sommer::mmes(
      y ~ 1,
      random = ~
        vsm(
          ism(id),
          Gu = A_matrix
        ) +
        vsm(
          ism(idd),
          Gu = D_matrix
        ),
      rcov = ~ units,
      nIters = N_ITERS_SOMMER,
      tolParConvLL = TOL_LLIK,
      data = dat,
      verbose = FALSE,
      dateWarning = FALSE
    )

  } else {

    fit <- sommer::mmes(
      y ~ 1,
      random = ~
        vsm(
          ism(id),
          Gu = A_matrix
        ) +
        vsm(
          ism(idd),
          Gu = D_matrix
        ) +
        vsm(
          ism(ide),
          Gu = E_matrix
        ),
      rcov = ~ units,
      nIters = N_ITERS_SOMMER,
      tolParConvLL = TOL_LLIK,
      data = dat,
      verbose = FALSE,
      dateWarning = FALSE
    )
  }

  fit_seconds <-
    proc.time()[[
      "elapsed"
    ]] -
    fit_start

  theta <- as.numeric(
    fit$theta
  )

  llik <- as.numeric(
    fit$llik
  )

  if (
    length(
      llik
    ) > 1L
  ) {

    last_llik_change <- tail(
      diff(
        llik
      ),
      1L
    )

  } else {

    last_llik_change <- NA_real_
  }

  variance_A <- 0
  variance_D <- 0
  variance_E <- 0
  variance_residual <- 0

  if (
    structure == "A"
  ) {

    stopifnot(
      length(
        theta
      ) == 2L
    )

    variance_A <- theta[
      1L
    ]

    variance_residual <- theta[
      2L
    ]

  } else if (
    structure == "AD"
  ) {

    stopifnot(
      length(
        theta
      ) == 3L
    )

    variance_A <- theta[
      1L
    ]

    variance_D <- theta[
      2L
    ]

    variance_residual <- theta[
      3L
    ]

  } else {

    stopifnot(
      length(
        theta
      ) == 4L
    )

    variance_A <- theta[
      1L
    ]

    variance_D <- theta[
      2L
    ]

    variance_E <- theta[
      3L
    ]

    variance_residual <- theta[
      4L
    ]
  }

  any_negative <- any(
    c(
      variance_A,
      variance_D,
      variance_E,
      variance_residual
    ) < 0
  )

  pass_llik_gate <-
    is.finite(
      last_llik_change
    ) &&
    abs(
      last_llik_change
    ) <= TOL_LLIK

  prediction_start <- proc.time()[[
    "elapsed"
  ]]

  additive <- rep(
    0,
    length(
      ids
    )
  )

  dominance <- rep(
    0,
    length(
      ids
    )
  )

  epistatic <- rep(
    0,
    length(
      ids
    )
  )

  additive_effect <- as.matrix(
    fit$uList[[
      "vsm(ism(id), Gu = A_matrix)"
    ]]
  )

  additive_incidence <- model.matrix(
    ~ id - 1,
    data = dat
  )

  additive <- as.numeric(
    additive_incidence %*%
      additive_effect[
        ,
        1L,
        drop = FALSE
      ]
  )

  if (
    structure %in%
      c(
        "AD",
        "ADE"
      )
  ) {

    dominance_effect <- as.matrix(
      fit$uList[[
        "vsm(ism(idd), Gu = D_matrix)"
      ]]
    )

    dominance_incidence <- model.matrix(
      ~ idd - 1,
      data = dat
    )

    dominance <- as.numeric(
      dominance_incidence %*%
        dominance_effect[
          ,
          1L,
          drop = FALSE
        ]
    )
  }

  if (
    structure == "ADE"
  ) {

    epistatic_effect <- as.matrix(
      fit$uList[[
        "vsm(ism(ide), Gu = E_matrix)"
      ]]
    )

    epistatic_incidence <- model.matrix(
      ~ ide - 1,
      data = dat
    )

    epistatic <- as.numeric(
      epistatic_incidence %*%
        epistatic_effect[
          ,
          1L,
          drop = FALSE
        ]
    )
  }

  genomic_component <-
    additive +
    dominance +
    epistatic

  intercept <- as.numeric(
    fit$b
  )[
    1L
  ]

  predicted_value <-
    intercept +
    genomic_component

  predict_seconds <-
    proc.time()[[
      "elapsed"
    ]] -
    prediction_start

  observed_test <- response_vector[
    assessment_index
  ]

  predicted_test <- predicted_value[
    assessment_index
  ]

  stopifnot(
    length(
      observed_test
    ) == 39L,
    length(
      predicted_test
    ) == 39L,
    all(
      is.finite(
        observed_test
      )
    ),
    all(
      is.finite(
        predicted_test
      )
    )
  )

  constant_prediction <-
    length(
      unique(
        predicted_test
      )
    ) == 1L

  if (
    length(
      unique(
        observed_test
      )
    ) > 1L &&
    !constant_prediction
  ) {

    correlation <- cor(
      predicted_test,
      observed_test,
      method = "pearson"
    )

    spearman <- cor(
      predicted_test,
      observed_test,
      method = "spearman"
    )

  } else {

    correlation <- NA_real_
    spearman <- NA_real_
  }

  rmse <- sqrt(
    mean(
      (
        predicted_test -
        observed_test
      )^2
    )
  )

  mae <- mean(
    abs(
      predicted_test -
      observed_test
    )
  )

  bias <- mean(
    predicted_test -
    observed_test
  )

  if (
    !constant_prediction
  ) {

    slope <- as.numeric(
      coef(
        lm(
          observed_test ~
            predicted_test
        )
      )[
        2L
      ]
    )

  } else {

    slope <- NA_real_
  }

  result_list[[
    i
  ]] <- data.frame(
    Dataset = "real",
    Trait = trait,
    Repetition = task$Repetition,
    Fold = task$OuterFold,
    SplitID = task$SplitID,
    TaskID = task$TaskID,
    Model = task$Model,
    Structure = structure,
    N_train = length(
      analysis_index
    ),
    N_test = length(
      assessment_index
    ),
    Convergence = isTRUE(
      fit$convergence
    ),
    Iterations = length(
      llik
    ),
    Final_LLik = tail(
      llik,
      1L
    ),
    Last_LLik_change =
      last_llik_change,
    Pass_LLik_gate =
      pass_llik_gate,
    Variance_A =
      variance_A,
    Variance_D =
      variance_D,
    Variance_E =
      variance_E,
    Variance_Residual =
      variance_residual,
    Any_negative =
      any_negative,
    Constant_prediction =
      constant_prediction,
    BLUP_Correlation =
      correlation,
    BLUP_Spearman =
      spearman,
    BLUP_RMSE =
      rmse,
    BLUP_MAE =
      mae,
    BLUP_Bias =
      bias,
    BLUP_Slope =
      slope,
    Kernel_build_seconds =
      kernel_seconds,
    Fit_seconds =
      fit_seconds,
    Predict_seconds =
      predict_seconds,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  prediction_list[[
    i
  ]] <- data.frame(
    Dataset = "real",
    Trait = trait,
    Repetition = task$Repetition,
    Fold = task$OuterFold,
    SplitID = task$SplitID,
    TaskID = task$TaskID,
    Model = task$Model,
    Structure = structure,
    ID = ids[
      assessment_index
    ],
    Observed_BLUP =
      observed_test,
    Predicted_BLUP =
      predicted_test,
    Genomic_Component =
      genomic_component[
        assessment_index
      ],
    Additive_Prediction =
      additive[
        assessment_index
      ],
    Dominance_Prediction =
      dominance[
        assessment_index
      ],
    Epistatic_Prediction =
      epistatic[
        assessment_index
      ],
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  cat(
    sprintf(
      "[%03d/%03d] %s | conv=%s | neg=%s | LL=%s | Pearson=%s | Spearman=%s | RMSE=%.4f\n",
      i,
      nrow(
        task_table
      ),
      task$TaskID,
      isTRUE(
        fit$convergence
      ),
      any_negative,
      pass_llik_gate,
      ifelse(
        is.finite(
          correlation
        ),
        sprintf(
          "%.4f",
          correlation
        ),
        "NA"
      ),
      ifelse(
        is.finite(
          spearman
        ),
        sprintf(
          "%.4f",
          spearman
        ),
        "NA"
      ),
      rmse
    )
  )
}

results <- do.call(

)

predictions <- do.call(

)
```

## 8. Numerical behavior

The numerical diagnostics are reported because they help interpret model
complexity. They are not used to replace one candidate structure by another
within a validation split.

```{r numerical-summary}
numerical_summary <- data.frame(
  Structure = character(0),
  Trait = character(0),
  Fits = integer(0),
  Converged = integer(0),
  Negative_components = integer(0),
  Pass_LLik_gate = integer(0),
  Constant_predictions = integer(0),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

for (
  structure in
    c(
      "A",
      "AD",
      "ADE"
    )
) {

  for (
    trait in
      traits
  ) {

    x <- results[
      results$Structure ==
        structure &
        results$Trait ==
        trait,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    numerical_summary <- rbind(
      numerical_summary,
      data.frame(
        Structure =
          structure,
        Trait =
          trait,
        Fits =
          nrow(
            x
          ),
        Converged =
          sum(
            x$Convergence
          ),
        Negative_components =
          sum(
            x$Any_negative
          ),
        Pass_LLik_gate =
          sum(
            x$Pass_LLik_gate
          ),
        Constant_predictions =
          sum(
            x$Constant_prediction
          ),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    )
  }
}

write.csv(
  numerical_summary,
  NUMERICAL_SUMMARY_CSV,
  row.names = FALSE
)

numerical_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Numerical behavior of the fixed GBLUP structures",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%;"'
  )
```

A variance component estimated near the boundary can be numerically difficult
for a more complex covariance structure. These diagnostics are therefore
interpreted together with held-out predictive performance rather than as a
criterion for changing the model assigned to a specific split.

## 9. Held-out predictive performance

Pearson and Spearman correlations and the calibration slope are undefined
when all 39 held-out predictions from a task are constant. RMSE, MAE, and bias
remain defined in those tasks. Each metric is therefore summarized from all
tasks for which that specific metric is finite.

```{r performance-summary}
performance_summary <- data.frame(
  Structure = character(0),
  Model = character(0),
  Trait = character(0),
  Splits = integer(0),
  Correlation_N = integer(0),
  BLUP_Correlation = numeric(0),
  BLUP_Correlation_SD = numeric(0),
  Spearman_N = integer(0),
  BLUP_Spearman = numeric(0),
  BLUP_Spearman_SD = numeric(0),
  RMSE_N = integer(0),
  BLUP_RMSE = numeric(0),
  MAE_N = integer(0),
  BLUP_MAE = numeric(0),
  Bias_N = integer(0),
  BLUP_Bias = numeric(0),
  Slope_N = integer(0),
  BLUP_Slope = numeric(0),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

for (
  structure in
    c(
      "A",
      "AD",
      "ADE"
    )
) {

  for (
    trait in
      traits
  ) {

    x <- results[
      results$Structure ==
        structure &
        results$Trait ==
        trait,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    model_name <- unique(
      x$Model
    )

    stopifnot(
      length(
        model_name
      ) == 1L
    )

    performance_summary <- rbind(
      performance_summary,
      data.frame(
        Structure =
          structure,
        Model =
          model_name,
        Trait =
          trait,
        Splits =
          nrow(
            x
          ),
        Correlation_N =
          sum(
            is.finite(
              x$BLUP_Correlation
            )
          ),
        BLUP_Correlation =
          mean(
            x$BLUP_Correlation,
            na.rm = TRUE
          ),
        BLUP_Correlation_SD =
          sd(
            x$BLUP_Correlation,
            na.rm = TRUE
          ),
        Spearman_N =
          sum(
            is.finite(
              x$BLUP_Spearman
            )
          ),
        BLUP_Spearman =
          mean(
            x$BLUP_Spearman,
            na.rm = TRUE
          ),
        BLUP_Spearman_SD =
          sd(
            x$BLUP_Spearman,
            na.rm = TRUE
          ),
        RMSE_N =
          sum(
            is.finite(
              x$BLUP_RMSE
            )
          ),
        BLUP_RMSE =
          mean(
            x$BLUP_RMSE,
            na.rm = TRUE
          ),
        MAE_N =
          sum(
            is.finite(
              x$BLUP_MAE
            )
          ),
        BLUP_MAE =
          mean(
            x$BLUP_MAE,
            na.rm = TRUE
          ),
        Bias_N =
          sum(
            is.finite(
              x$BLUP_Bias
            )
          ),
        BLUP_Bias =
          mean(
            x$BLUP_Bias,
            na.rm = TRUE
          ),
        Slope_N =
          sum(
            is.finite(
              x$BLUP_Slope
            )
          ),
        BLUP_Slope =
          mean(
            x$BLUP_Slope,
            na.rm = TRUE
          ),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    )
  }
}

write.csv(
  performance_summary,
  PERFORMANCE_SUMMARY_CSV,
  row.names = FALSE
)

performance_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Mean held-out performance of A, AD, and ADE across the 25 outer splits",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%;"'
  )
```

The comparison is intentionally descriptive at this stage. A more complete
cross-model comparison, including the regularized ANN models, is performed in
the final comparison module.

## 10. Out-of-fold ranking of the 195 individuals

Each individual is assessed once in every repetition and therefore has five
held-out predictions for each trait and GBLUP structure. These five out-of-fold
predictions are averaged before the global ranking is constructed. This yields
one predictive value per individual, model, and trait using only predictions
obtained while that individual was outside the training set.

Ranks are defined in decreasing order: rank 1 corresponds to the highest BLUP.
The absolute rank error measures the displacement between the observed and
predicted ordering.

Selection agreement is also evaluated for the upper 20% of the population.
With 195 individuals, the selected group contains exactly 39 individuals.
When BLUP values are tied at the selection boundary, `ID` is used only as a
deterministic secondary ordering criterion so that both observed and predicted
sets contain exactly 39 individuals.

```{r individual-ranking}
TOP20_N <- 39L

individual_ranking <- data.frame(
  Structure = character(0),
  Model = character(0),
  Trait = character(0),
  ID = character(0),
  Observed_BLUP = numeric(0),
  Predicted_BLUP = numeric(0),
  Prediction_SD = numeric(0),
  N_OOF = integer(0),
  Observed_Rank = numeric(0),
  Predicted_Rank = numeric(0),
  Rank_Difference = numeric(0),
  Absolute_Rank_Error = numeric(0),
  Observed_Top20 = logical(0),
  Predicted_Top20 = logical(0),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

ranking_summary <- data.frame(
  Structure = character(0),
  Model = character(0),
  Trait = character(0),
  Individuals = integer(0),
  Ranking_Spearman = numeric(0),
  Mean_Absolute_Rank_Error = numeric(0),
  Median_Absolute_Rank_Error = numeric(0),
  Top20_N = integer(0),
  Top20_Overlap_N = integer(0),
  Top20_Overlap_Rate = numeric(0),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

for (
  structure in
    c(
      "A",
      "AD",
      "ADE"
    )
) {

  for (
    trait in
      traits
  ) {

    x <- predictions[
      predictions$Structure ==
        structure &
        predictions$Trait ==
        trait,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    model_name <- unique(
      x$Model
    )

    stopifnot(
      length(
        model_name
      ) == 1L
    )

    ranking_group <- data.frame(
      Structure = character(0),
      Model = character(0),
      Trait = character(0),
      ID = character(0),
      Observed_BLUP = numeric(0),
      Predicted_BLUP = numeric(0),
      Prediction_SD = numeric(0),
      N_OOF = integer(0),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )

    for (
      individual_id in
        ids
    ) {

      xi <- x[
        x$ID ==
          individual_id,
        ,
        drop = FALSE
      ]

      stopifnot(
        nrow(
          xi
        ) == 5L,
        length(
          unique(
            xi$Observed_BLUP
          )
        ) == 1L
      )

      ranking_group <- rbind(
        ranking_group,
        data.frame(
          Structure =
            structure,
          Model =
            model_name,
          Trait =
            trait,
          ID =
            individual_id,
          Observed_BLUP =
            unique(
              xi$Observed_BLUP
            ),
          Predicted_BLUP =
            mean(
              xi$Predicted_BLUP
            ),
          Prediction_SD =
            sd(
              xi$Predicted_BLUP
            ),
          N_OOF =
            nrow(
              xi
            ),
          stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )
      )
    }

    ranking_group$Observed_Rank <- rank(
      -ranking_group$Observed_BLUP,
      ties.method = "average"
    )

    ranking_group$Predicted_Rank <- rank(
      -ranking_group$Predicted_BLUP,
      ties.method = "average"
    )

    ranking_group$Rank_Difference <-
      ranking_group$Predicted_Rank -
      ranking_group$Observed_Rank

    ranking_group$Absolute_Rank_Error <-
      abs(
        ranking_group$Rank_Difference
      )

    observed_order <- order(
      -ranking_group$Observed_BLUP,
      ranking_group$ID
    )

    predicted_order <- order(
      -ranking_group$Predicted_BLUP,
      ranking_group$ID
    )

    ranking_group$Observed_Top20 <- FALSE
    ranking_group$Predicted_Top20 <- FALSE

    ranking_group$Observed_Top20[
      observed_order[
        seq_len(
          TOP20_N
        )
      ]
    ] <- TRUE

    ranking_group$Predicted_Top20[
      predicted_order[
        seq_len(
          TOP20_N
        )
      ]
    ] <- TRUE

    top20_overlap_n <- sum(
      ranking_group$Observed_Top20 &
        ranking_group$Predicted_Top20
    )

    top20_overlap_rate <-
      top20_overlap_n /
      TOP20_N

    stopifnot(
      nrow(
        ranking_group
      ) == 195L,
      all(
        ranking_group$N_OOF ==
          5L
      ),
      sum(
        ranking_group$Observed_Top20
      ) == TOP20_N,
      sum(
        ranking_group$Predicted_Top20
      ) == TOP20_N,
      top20_overlap_n >= 0L,
      top20_overlap_n <= TOP20_N
    )

    individual_ranking <- rbind(
      individual_ranking,
      ranking_group
    )

    ranking_summary <- rbind(
      ranking_summary,
      data.frame(
        Structure =
          structure,
        Model =
          model_name,
        Trait =
          trait,
        Individuals =
          nrow(
            ranking_group
          ),
        Ranking_Spearman =
          cor(
            ranking_group$Observed_Rank,
            ranking_group$Predicted_Rank,
            method = "spearman"
          ),
        Mean_Absolute_Rank_Error =
          mean(
            ranking_group$Absolute_Rank_Error
          ),
        Median_Absolute_Rank_Error =
          median(
            ranking_group$Absolute_Rank_Error
          ),
        Top20_N =
          TOP20_N,
        Top20_Overlap_N =
          top20_overlap_n,
        Top20_Overlap_Rate =
          top20_overlap_rate,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    )
  }
}

rownames(
  individual_ranking
) <- NULL

rownames(
  ranking_summary
) <- NULL

stopifnot(
  nrow(
    individual_ranking
  ) == 1755L,
  nrow(
    ranking_summary
  ) == 9L,
  all(
    individual_ranking$N_OOF ==
      5L
  ),
  sum(
    individual_ranking$Observed_Top20
  ) == 351L,
  sum(
    individual_ranking$Predicted_Top20
  ) == 351L,
  all(
    ranking_summary$Top20_N ==
      39L
  ),
  all(
    ranking_summary$Top20_Overlap_N >=
      0L
  ),
  all(
    ranking_summary$Top20_Overlap_N <=
      39L
  ),
  all(
    ranking_summary$Top20_Overlap_Rate >=
      0
  ),
  all(
    ranking_summary$Top20_Overlap_Rate <=
      1
  )
)

write.csv(
  individual_ranking,
  RANKING_CSV,
  row.names = FALSE
)

saveRDS(
  individual_ranking,
  RANKING_RDS
)

write.csv(
  ranking_summary,
  RANKING_SUMMARY_CSV,
  row.names = FALSE
)

ranking_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Agreement between observed and out-of-fold predicted rankings of the 195 individuals",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%;"'
  )
```

The ranking summary complements split-level Spearman correlation by evaluating
the ordering obtained from the five out-of-fold predictions available for each
individual. The top-20% overlap additionally measures how many of the 39
individuals selected from observed BLUPs are recovered by the out-of-fold
predicted ranking.

```{r final-integrity-check}
  all(
    ranking_summary$Top20_Overlap_Rate >=
      0
  ),
  all(
    ranking_summary$Top20_Overlap_Rate <=
      1
  )
)

for (
  trait in
    traits
) {

  for (
    structure in
      c(
        "A",
        "AD",
        "ADE"
      )
  ) {

    x <- predictions[
      predictions$Trait ==
        trait &
        predictions$Structure ==
        structure,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    frequency <- table(
      x$ID
    )

    stopifnot(
      length(
        frequency
      ) == 195L,
      min(
        frequency
      ) == 5L,
      max(
        frequency
      ) == 5L
    )
  }
}
```

The three fixed GBLUP structures are now ready for comparison with the
regularized ANN models under the same outer validation design.
